prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: parking lot collision in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1211; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage does not match the story: the dents are on another side and at another height than the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a collision in a parking lot in Houston, Texas, where Driver 1 reported a wrist fracture from the impact. Driver 1 was seated in the vehicle when officers arrived, and Passenger, who was also present, confirmed this. The injury described is consistent with the force expected from a collision of this type. Photographs taken at the scene show some of the details Driver 1 described, but no independent witnesses were located. On inspection, the damage to Driver 2's vehicle sits on a different side and at a different height than the impact Driver 1 described, and the account given does not fully match the damage observed. No prior damage to the vehicle was known to officers or to the parties. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the policy covering the vehicle. Officers documented the scene, collected the photographs, and recorded statements from all parties present for the follow-up review.
